policy_title: Enforce a 2-strike rule for job offers for benefit claimants
stated: Reform UK will enforce a 2-strike rule where all job seekers and those fit to work must find employment within four months or accept a job after two offers, otherwise, benefits will be withdrawn.

source.quote: Enforce a 2-Strike Rule for Job Offers All job seekers and those fit to work must find employment within 4 months or accept a job after 2 offers. Otherwise, benefits are withdrawn.

bearing_set.reason: Withdrawal of benefits directly removes disposable income for affected claimants, materially affecting their ability to afford essentials — a real verdict on cost-of-living adequacy for the relevant population.

The policy compels acceptance of any offered job within a strict timeframe, directly shaping employment quality, job security, and conditions for claimants — a real verdict on whether people can earn a decent, secure living.

The policy uses withdrawal of income support as a mechanism to coerce acceptance of specific jobs, imposing a concrete state-mandated constraint on individual economic choice and freedom from coercion.
Reducing the number of benefit recipients has a direct, material effect on welfare expenditure and the funded/borrowed balance in public finances; a genuine fiscal verdict is earned here.
Moving claimants into employment raises labour-force participation and aggregate output, bearing on productivity and real living-standards indicators, though mismatched placements could offset gains.

The policy bears almost entirely on the lowest income group; benefit withdrawal and forced low-quality job placement risk widening the income gap between the poorest and the rest, earning a real inequality verdict.

membership_note: Six fundamentals earn real verdicts: two on the worker/claimant experience (O2 absolute affordability, O4 job quality), two on systemic effects (O12 fiscal, O13 aggregate prosperity), one on liberty (O10 state coercion), and one on distribution (O14 inequality gap). O9 is not included because the policy as stated does not target a specific protected characteristic or democratic right; O5 and O15 have at most incidental and speculative mechanisms at this level of policy detail.
